result.title: Preface
result.summary: The August 2026 San Diego City Employees’ Retirement System RFP seeks a General Investment Consultant. Its contents cover the introduction; proposal participation, completion, and submission procedures, including mandatory requirements and minimum-requirements certification, confidentiality, intent to participate, and submission; evaluation criteria; insurance requirements; required services; and the technical proposal. Technical proposal sections address firm profile, organization and people, investment philosophy and process, services and fees, other information, and a response checklist.

result.title: I. Introduction
result.summary:
I. Introduction
The San Diego City Employees' Retirement System (SDCERS) is requesting proposals from general investment consultants to provide comprehensive pension fund investment consulting services. SDCERS is seeking proposals from independent general investment consultants who have consulting experience in the public pension fund area. Firms are invited to participate in an evaluation process to further represent their capabilities of rendering the following consultant services:
Investment Policy Asset Allocation and Portfolio Oversight Investment Manager Oversight Performance Measurement Training, Education and Client Service
See section V. for further details on each service area.

result.title: II. Proposal Participation, Completion and Submission Procedures
key_items: A. Mandatory Requirements Certification and Minimum Requirements
result.summary: The RFP section sets minimum qualifications for general investment consulting firms as of January 1, 2027. Firms must complete Attachment A, the Mandatory Requirements Certification, and submit it with the cover letter. Requirements include: registration as an investment adviser under the Investment Company Act of 1940, with ADV I and II and schedules provided as Exhibit A; substantial experience advising multibillion-dollar public pension systems; at least five continuous years of general investment consulting for large institutional clients; and, at the firm’s expense, an electronic reporting interface with SDCERS’ custodian, State Street Bank. Firms must disclose actual and potential conflicts and annually report non-consulting revenue sources and affiliations, follow SDCERS’ conflict and placement-agent policies, and promptly notify the CIO of material conflicts. The firm must directly manage the account using its own employees, have no material conflicts involving SDCERS-related parties, maintain required insurance, and have its principal place of business in the United States and be subject to U.S. service of process.

result.title: B. Confidentiality
result.summary: RFP responses become SDCERS property and remain confidential until a contract award recommendation is announced; afterward, they may be publicly inspected or disclosed under applicable law, including the California Public Records Act. If a proposal is requested, SDCERS will notify the proposer’s authorized representative before responding. The proposer alone must assert any exemption and obtain a judicial determination; SDCERS will not do so, and documents are publicly available absent such a determination. Submitting a proposal waives claims against SDCERS and its agents, Board members, officers, or employees for privacy violations, trade-secret disclosure, or damage resulting from inspection or copying.

result.title: C. Intention to Participate
result.summary:
C. Intention to Participate
If you intend to reply to the RFP, please send an e-mail to Carina Coleman (ccoleman@sdcers.gov), Anders Norrman (anorrman@sdcers.gov) Jamie Hamrick (jhamrick@sdcers.gov), and Demitrios Haldes (dhaldes@sdcers.gov), attaching a letter that your organization will be replying to the RFP. If you have any questions, please e- mail Carina Coleman, Anders Norrman, Jamie Hamrick, and Demitrios Haldes.

result.title: D. RFP Submission
result.summary: Proposals must answer Technical Proposal questions in order, prefacing each response with its section and question numbers and text; extra information may go in an appendix. SDCERS is not responsible for proposal-preparation costs. Responses must include a signed cover letter from someone authorized to bind the firm, with the signer’s title; unsigned letters may result in rejection. The letter must acknowledge that submitted documents become public records and provide the proposer’s contact details, federal employer and applicable corporate identification numbers, authorization to bind, primary contact details if different, an irrevocable six-month offer statement, willingness to perform the described services, and confirmation of staff and resources to meet timelines and deliverables. Attach the Fee Proposal as Exhibit D. The text also identifies key search milestones for a deadlines table: RFP issuance, questions and responses, proposal submission, evaluation, interview scheduling and interviews, on-site due diligence, finalist presentations, contract negotiation and execution, and commencement of work; no dates are shown.

result.title: Deadline Date
result.summary: The RFP timeline lists August 11, 18, and 26, 2026; the proposal deadline of September 22, 2026, at 5:00 PM PDT; September 23–October 5, October 6–11, and October 12–23, 2026; November 2–13, 2026; a January 2027 meeting (date TBD); January–May 2027; and June 1, 2027. Proposals must be labeled “2026 SDCERS General Investment Consultant Search” and submitted electronically as a complete PDF by email to Chief Investment Officer Carina Coleman, with copies to the specified SDCERS addresses. Questions should be directed to the four designated RFP contacts. All materials must be received by the deadline; late proposals will not be accepted. A quiet period runs from RFP issuance until selection concludes in May 2027; proposers may contact only designated representatives about the RFP, and violations may result in disqualification.

result.title: III. Proposal Evaluation Criteria
result.summary: SDCERS will set the evaluation methodology and criteria, with its staff having sole and exclusive discretion to assess minimum qualifications, candidate suitability, and finalist selection. General considerations include understanding the scope of services; timely delivery; independence and objectivity; firm and client experience; analytical tools, research, and process; personnel and proposed consultant team; client and industry feedback; and fees. Compensation is important, but SDCERS need not select the lowest-cost bidder; the Board will choose, in its sole discretion, the firm that best serves plan participants and beneficiaries.

result.title: IV. Insurance Requirements
result.summary:
IV. Insurance Requirements
The selected firm shall provide evidence of Professional Liability insurance with contractual liability coverage covering the Proposer’s liability arising from errors and omissions (E&O) made directly or indirectly during the duration of the contract. The selected firm shall provide coverage for the total limits actually arranged by the selected firm but not less than a $10 million combined single limit, in addition to no less than $10 million of directors and officers (D&O) insurance.
The selected firm shall maintain a Fidelity Bond covering employee dishonesty, in an amount arranged by the selected firm, but not less than $15 million, per occurrence. In addition, the selected firm shall maintain workers compensation coverage. Finally, the selected firm shall maintain cybersecurity insurance not less than $5 million.

result.title: V. Scope of Services Required
result.summary: The consultant must advise on long-term investment policy, objectives, guidelines, proxy voting, risk management, compliance, and rebalancing. Duties include annual asset-allocation and Investment Policy Statement reviews, asset/liability studies at least every three years, annual manager-structure reviews, asset-class research, and analytical tools. The consultant must advise on securities lending, custody, vendor fees, and brokerage strategies, monitor securities-lending compliance, and analyze brokerage costs annually. Manager services include ongoing monitoring, research, selection, compliance and CFA-guideline oversight, allocation/structure and benchmark advice, and annual peer comparisons of fees. The consultant must report annually on ESG and emerging/diverse-manager efforts and address firm diversity, manager sourcing, due diligence, portfolio use, the share of such managers, and supporting resources. Performance duties cover portfolio and manager benchmarks, peer rankings, quarterly reports and reviews, benchmark analysis, and portfolio risk. Client services include meetings, coordination with specialists, education, special projects and workshops, regular communication, materials, timely responses, research access, and no consultant-team changes without SDCERS approval.

result.title: Section II - Organization / People
key_items: I. Indicate the number of consulting client relationships gained and lost in the last three years:
result.summary: Section II requests information about the consulting firm’s ownership, business plan, anticipated ownership changes, primary business and services, five-year growth objectives, near-term priorities, and planned client capacity. It seeks revenue percentages by service category for 2023–2025, latest-year financial condition, strengths, and client relationships gained and lost by year and fund type. Firms must identify terminated full-service retainer clients since 2023, assets and reasons; report client counts and assets under advisement for 2023–2025; and describe consulting-team experience, tenure, staffing changes, and SDCERS account responsibility. Applicants must provide principal staff education, credentials, recent and anticipated senior-staff changes, an organization chart (Exhibit B), and staff resumes (Exhibit C). They must disclose potential conflicts, including affiliate, broker-dealer, and investment-banking activities, and attach a conflicts policy and Code of Ethics (Exhibit D). The section also asks about staff compensation, retention incentives, links between client outcomes and consultant performance, and insurance/bonding coverage amounts and carriers.

result.title: Type of Coverage
key_items: V. Describe your firm’s disaster recovery plan.
result.summary: The form includes fields for type of coverage and dollar amount, then asks whether the firm is or has been reviewed or audited by the SEC or another regulator and, if so, for details; whether it has been censured by a regulator, with an explanation or “n/a”; and whether the firm or a proposed consulting-team principal has been involved in litigation or other legal proceedings in the past five years. Respondents must indicate yes or no and, if yes, attach an explanation and current status. The firm must describe its disaster recovery plan. Exhibit E must list current investment consulting clients, categorized by client type, and provide each relationship’s approximate asset value as of March 31, 2026, or current value, years of service, and whether services are retainer-based or special projects only. Client-type subtotals and a firm-wide total of relationship values are required.

result.title: Section III – Philosophy & Process
result.summary: Section III requests the firm to explain its investment-consulting philosophy and processes for developing and reviewing pension investment policies, including timing and client-specific factors; analyzing manager structure; and managing public-pension risks, particularly negative cash flow. It covers manager searches and selection criteria, ongoing manager monitoring beyond returns and termination considerations, operational due diligence and dedicated resources, research staffing and on-site visits, and reviews of firms, products, news, and headline risk. It asks about client research reports, topics, authors, frequency, annual publications, information sources, and a sample report. It also addresses how ESG and DEI inform recommendations, available expertise, and review frequency; views on passive versus active management across sectors and public versus private markets; benchmark selection and custom benchmarks; and appropriate performance-reporting methodologies by asset class.

result.title: Section IV – Services Offered / Fees
result.summary:
Section IV – Services Offered / Fees
A. Review the scope of general investment consulting services sought in the cover letter and questionnaire cover, and list which of the services your firm is capable of providing.
B. Indicate any special resources or tools utilized in providing the above identified services that would give your firm a competitive advantage over other general investment consulting firms.
C. Indicate the fee structure for providing the services listed in the scope of general investment consulting services. In order to assist SDCERS in standardizing the comparison of quoted fee structures, please indicate a full retainer annual dollar cost for performing all of these services. If your firm is unable to provide an all-inclusive full retainer fee proposal, then separately identify and price those components of the scope of duties (such as RFPs for manager searches) that would be billed on a per project basis.
